scenes.narration: Solar cells convert light energy into electrical energy.

content.body: From incoming light to useful electricity.

scenes.title: Follow the energy conversion
scenes.narration: Panels produce DC electricity. An inverter converts it to AC for household use.

source.label: U.S. DOE · Solar Photovoltaic Technology Basics

scenes.title: DC and AC describe different behavior
scenes.narration: DC maintains a direction of current. AC periodically reverses direction.

content.subtitle: A conceptual comparison; actual waveforms can vary

items.label: Direct current
items.detail: The direction of current does not periodically reverse. PV panels supply DC.

items.label: Alternating current
items.detail: Current periodically reverses direction. Grid-connected homes commonly use AC.

scenes.title: Power and time determine energy
scenes.narration: At constant power, two kilowatts for three hours gives six kilowatt-hours.

scenes.title: The three ideas to remember
scenes.narration: Light becomes DC electricity. Inverters provide AC. Energy depends on power and time.

content.subtitle: Simplified explanation; not an installation guide

items.label: Solar cells convert incoming light into electrical energy.
An inverter converts DC electricity into AC.
For constant power, energy equals power multiplied by time.
